date_note: Malicious versions published Nov 17; reported Nov 18.
title: Microsoft Agent Framework PyPI package compromised with credential stealer
summary: Versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 of the agent-framework package on PyPI were published on November 17 with a credential stealer that runs when Python starts, targeting cloud, GitHub and AI credentials and tokens. PyPI quarantined both; 1.26.0 is the last safe version. Italy's CSIRT (ACN) says the malware installed no OS-level persistence and downloaded no further payloads. Xakep.ru reports Microsoft said it made some repositories private during the investigation; the entry route is unknown.
plain: Two bad releases of a popular Microsoft AI package were uploaded to PyPI. Anyone who installed them may have had cloud and developer passwords and tokens stolen.
exec: A trusted package on an official Microsoft project carried a credential stealer; any build or developer machine that installed it may have exposed cloud access.
action: Wiz and CSIRT Italia advise pinning agent-framework to 1.26.0, checking lockfiles, CI logs and environments for 1.26.1 or 1.26.2, and rotating credentials and tokens exposed to any host that installed them.

key_findings: Malicious 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 ran a credential stealer at Python startup, even without importing the package.
Targets include Azure, AWS, GitHub, Docker, Hugging Face and OpenAI credentials and cloud identity tokens; data went to a webhook.site endpoint.
PyPI quarantined both releases; how the attacker got publish access is not known.

validation.note: Compared BleepingComputer with Wiz and Socket (independent vendor analyses): versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2, November 17, .pth credential stealer, 1.26.0 safe; Wiz states both removed from PyPI about 21:30 UTC. Download figure rests on BleepingComputer only.

review.note: Action did not name its source: now attributed to Wiz and CSIRT Italia. Removed occurred_at 20:35 (no evidence quote). Added published days for BleepingComputer, Wiz and ACN. Versions, dates, targets, ACN no-persistence and Xakep repositories-private checked. Socket, ITmedia and Infobae not opened.
